key_insight: A two-stage deep learning pipeline jointly cancels narrowband interference and produces reliable soft LLRs for OFDM, fixing the mismatch between classical interference suppression and Gaussian demodulation.
engineering_relevance: It offers a lower-latency, more scalable receiver-side solution that improves BLER and avoids error floors under strong or overlapping interference.
method: NBI-CNet uses a physics-informed CNN to estimate and subtract multi-tone narrowband interference in one forward pass.
LLR-CNet whitens non-Gaussian residuals into calibrated soft metrics for robust demodulation.
The design is scale-invariant and does not require prior knowledge of the number of interferers.
evidence_signal: Simulations show up to 60% complexity reduction versus EOMP-IDS, near-optimal performance within 0.2 to 0.5 dB at BLER 10^-4 under SIR = -10 dB, and more than 3 dB coding gain under mild interference with heavy spectral overlap.
watch_item: Generalization depends on training coverage and careful integration with the receiver chain, especially when interference statistics differ from the simulated conditions.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Joint Narrowband Interference Cancellation and Soft Demodulation in OFDM Systems
